newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka promises end to blackouts.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka promises end to blackouts.

text.p: Sri Lanka, which suffered crippling power cuts last year, will double its thermal electricity generation by next month to ensure an end to power outages, a top government official said on Saturday.
"We can now very confidently state that the prospects of present and future power cuts are non-existent," Thilan Wijesinghe, chairman of the Board of Investment (BOI) told a news conference.

Wijesinghe, a member of the power committee appointed by President Chandrika Kumaratunga to tackle the island's power crisis, said new thermal electricity plants would come on stream by June, reducing the country's dependence on rain-fed hydropower plants.

"On account of the recent rainfalls, as well as this new power that is coming on stream and what is planned from 1998 onwards, I can confidently state that power shortages can be considered a thing of the past," he said.
Sri Lanka, which relies on hydropower to supply 83 percent of its electricity requirement, experienced a severe drought last year, forcing the government to introduce daily eight-hour power cuts.
The blackouts slashed industrial output and even forced some small industries to shut down.
A repeat of last year's drought was avoided after delayed inter-monsoon rains arrived in late April.
The Meteorological Department says the southwest monsoon, the most important for fuelling hydroelectric plants, was expected to break over Sri Lanka on time around the third week of May.
Wijesinghe said the dependence on hydropower would be reduced to 70 percent once a 115-megawatt gas turbine and a 40-megawatt diesel plant are commissioned.
The state power utility Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) says it plans to cut hydropower dependence to 57 percent of the requirement by building more thermal power plants.
The CEB also has plans to construct a 300 megawatt coal-fired power plant in the northwest, to be commissioned by the year 2000.
The island now has an installed capacity of 1,135 megawatts of hydroelectric power and 250 megawatts of thermal power.
